page: Microsoft Azure E32as_v4 is a memory-optimized instance engineered for workloads demanding high memory capacity per core. Built on the x86_64 architecture and running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the server is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz. It provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 256.0 GB, yielding a high ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Hardware capabilities also include 550 GB of bundled local SSD storage. The instance operates without discrete GPU hardware, relying entirely on the AMD EPYC CPU for processing tasks. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, BMI2, and FMA, although advanced vector extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX are not supported on this platform.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core and memory subsystem capabilities. The instance achieved a top-tier stress-ng single-core score of 2,707.99 and a PassMark memory score of 2,782.36. Text generation for small 135M language models reached 310.9 tokens per second, placing it in the top 25% of tested configurations. Multi-core performance metrics, such as a PassMark CPU score of 38,136.18, a Geekbench multi-core score of 14,393.0, and 31.48 million Redis SET operations per second, consistently place it within the middle 50% tier. Large-model LLM prompt processing shows lower throughput, with a 70B model registering 6.62 tokens per second.

Given its 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation and strong memory benchmarks, the Azure E32as_v4 provides cost-effective resource utilization for memory-bound systems rather than heavy parallel matrix computing. The server is well positioned for enterprise relational databases, large-scale in-memory caches, data analytics pipelines, and memory-heavy web application tiers.
